name: OnPace
subtitle: Late or Early at Every Stop
summary: Know at every checkpoint whether you are ahead of your plan or behind it

hero.hook: Know at every checkpoint whether you are ahead of your plan or behind it
hero.shotAlt: The OnPace trip screen. How far you are ahead of or behind plan shows in large minutes and seconds, and dots on a thin line mark the checkpoints and where you are now.

sections.title: How late, checkpoint by checkpoint
body: Set the times you pass a few points on the way: leaving home, the corner, the bus stop, the office. While you move, OnPace compares where you are with where the plan says you should be and shows the gap in minutes and seconds, in large type. It does not give directions. It tells you whether to hurry.
bullets: Minutes and seconds ahead of or behind plan
The next checkpoint and the time to pass it
Estimated arrival

visual.alt: The trip screen. The gap shows in large type, with the next checkpoint, its window and the estimated arrival alongside.
visual.caption: Close view of the app

sections.title: Routes from the map, or from one trip
body: Choose a departure and a destination and Apple Maps finds a walking or driving route, with checkpoints filled in along longer stretches. For a route no map can find, like a company shuttle, take it once and build the route from the trip. The places you stopped and where you got on and off become checkpoint candidates.
bullets: Walking and driving routes
A route built from a trip you take
A window of its own at each checkpoint

visual.alt: Making a route. The route found on the map, with checkpoints placed along it.
visual.caption: Close view of the app

sections.title: Without taking out your phone
body: During a trip the Lock Screen card and the Dynamic Island show the gap and the next checkpoint. Drift out of the window and you get one alert. Start from Control Center or Siri, and the trip stops on its own two minutes after you arrive.
bullets: Lock Screen card and Dynamic Island
An alert when you drift out of the window
Start from Control Center or Siri

sections.title: Tuned from your trips
body: Each trip adds real times. OnPace looks at the median of your recent trips and suggests moving a checkpoint you always reach late, or loosening a leg that is too tight. Moving your departure earlier from a single trip is open to everyone.

pro.title:
Routes without a limit,
and checkpoint times tuned from your trips
items: Routes without a limit (two to begin with)
Tune from trips: apply the suggestions to your checkpoint times

faq.q: The location arrow stays after a trip
a: OnPace uses location together with the Lock Screen card while a trip runs, and stops when you tap Stop or two minutes after you arrive. If the app is force-quit or reinstalled in the middle of a trip, iOS can keep the indicator. Restarting the phone clears it.
While Using the App is enough. Always is not needed. During a trip the Lock Screen card stays up, so location keeps coming with the screen off or another app open.

faq.q: The Lock Screen card doesn't appear
a: Turn on Settings > OnPace > Live Activities. If the card can't be shown, the app sends a notification instead, as long as notifications are on.
Turn on Transit to the next checkpoint on a checkpoint. When the signal drops underground, the gap you boarded with carries until you get off. Live bus and subway data is not used.
Put two checkpoints at the same place with their times apart, and that becomes a waiting leg. Arrive early and it shows Wait here until it is time to go.
Recently Deleted on the home screen keeps the last three routes you deleted. Tap Recover to bring one back. A recovered route counts toward your routes again.
Tap Restore purchase on the purchase screen. Family Sharing is on, so your family can use it too.

privacy.title: OnPace Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: OnPace collects no personal data. There is no account and no sign-in. Your routes and trips are kept on your device, and Apple handles place search, directions and the Pro purchase.
intro: kvndh (the developer) handles the personal data of users of the OnPace app (the app) as described below.

sections.title: Purposes of processing
paragraphs: The app has no sign-up or login, and the developer does not process personal information about its users. The app uses your location to compare your position with your plan and to show where you are on the map, and this happens on your device.

sections.title: Personal information processed
paragraphs: The developer collects no personal information. The app works with the data below, all of it kept in the app's storage on your device. The developer does not receive any of it.
bullets: Routes (name, the name, place and time of each checkpoint, windows, route shape): used to work out how far ahead or behind you are
Trip history (the planned and actual time at each checkpoint): used to make the Tune from trips suggestions
The track of your last trip (locations): used to draw the way you went when you build a route from a trip or tune from this trip

Diagnostic log (locations and times, and the activity type such as walking or driving with its confidence): used to look back at how the app behaved. It rolls over to a new log at 20 MB, and the release version has no way to export it
Settings and whether Pro was bought: used to lay out the app and decide which features open

sections.title: Retention period
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal data. Everything in the app's storage is removed when the app is deleted. Routes stay until you delete them, and trip history is cleared with Clear history in the app's settings. Deleted routes wait in Recently Deleted, which keeps the last three.

sections.title: Provision to third parties
paragraphs: Personal information is not provided to third parties.

sections.title: Outsourcing of processing
paragraphs: No processing is outsourced. The OnPace Pro purchase is handled by Apple on the App Store, and payment information follows Apple's privacy policy. Place search, walking and driving directions and the map are handled by Apple Maps and follow Apple's privacy policy. The developer receives no payment method, no Apple Account information and nothing you search for.

sections.title: Destruction of personal information
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal data, so there is nothing to destroy. A route you delete goes to Recently Deleted, trip history is cleared with Clear history in the app's settings, and deleting the app removes everything in it.

sections.title: Rights of users and legal representatives
paragraphs: Because the developer holds no personal information about you, there is nothing to access, correct or delete. If you have questions, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Security measures
paragraphs: What the app uses sits as files in the app's storage on your device. The developer runs no server, and the app does not use iCloud. Location is asked for While Using the App only; background location is used only during a trip you start, and the Lock Screen card stays up the whole time. Motion and fitness data is used only to tell walking from riding. Notifications are local: made on the device and delivered on the device.

sections.title: Cookies and other automatic collection
paragraphs: The app uses no cookies, no advertising identifier and no analytics tools.

sections.title: Privacy officer
paragraphs: If you have questions about personal information, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Remedies
paragraphs: If you need advice about a privacy concern or help settling a dispute, you can contact the Korean bodies listed below. If you live outside Korea, you can also contact the data protection authority in your country.
bullets: Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: 1833-6972 in Korea (www.kopico.go.kr)
Personal Information Infringement Report Center: 118 in Korea (privacy.kisa.or.kr)
Supreme Prosecutors' Office: 1301 in Korea (www.spo.go.kr)
National Police Agency: 182 in Korea (ecrm.police.go.kr)
European Union and EEA: the data protection authority of your country (edpb.europa.eu)
United Kingdom: Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk)
United States: Federal Trade Commission (reportfraud.ftc.gov)
Other countries: the data protection or consumer protection authority where you live

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If this policy changes, this page will show the new text and its new effective date.
